aiItems.content:
What is kitchen art wall decor?

Kitchen art wall decor refers to prints, paintings, or illustrated artworks chosen specifically to hang in a kitchen or kitchen-diner space, adding personality, colour, and warmth to what is often a purely functional room. It can range from botanical prints and food-inspired illustrations to typographic quotes and abstract designs — anything that makes the kitchen feel more like a curated, lived-in home. In recent years, French Country and botanical styles have become especially popular choices, thanks to their timeless, relaxed quality that suits both traditional and contemporary kitchens. A well-chosen set of kitchen art wall decor can completely change the feel of the room, making it a more welcoming place to cook, eat, and gather. Sets of three prints are a particularly popular format because they create an instant, balanced gallery-wall look without the guesswork of curating individual pieces.

How to Hang Kitchen Art Wall Decor: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure the space: Find a clear stretch of wall — above a dining table, beside the cooker, or along a run of cabinets works well. Measure the width so you know how much room you have for all three prints side by side.

2. Decide on the layout before you hang: Lay all three prints out on the floor first and adjust the spacing until it looks right — usually 5 to 8 cm between each print is a good starting point. Take a photo so you can refer to it when you're up the ladder.

3. Find the right height: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level — around 145 to 155 cm from the floor is the standard guide. If you're hanging them above a piece of furniture, aim for 15 to 20 cm above the top of the furniture.

4. Mark and hang: Use a pencil to lightly mark where each hook or nail will go, double-check with a spirit level, and then hang the prints. Step back and adjust any that need a small nudge.

5. Style around them: Once they're up, bring in complementary textures — linen, wood, wicker, or a small potted herb — to tie the botanical, French Country feel together.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Our Kitchen Art Wall Decor Formats

Unframed Print — You receive the art print only, ready for you to pop into a frame of your choice. Great if you already have frames or want to match a very specific existing decor. Available in Luster art paper (slight sheen, vibrant tones) or Museum quality paper (smooth, matte, gallery-style finish).

Framed Print — The print comes already mounted and framed, ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saver and ideal if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper finishes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped tightly around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary, borderless look. Arrives ready to hang. No glass, no frame — just clean, textured botanical art on the wall. Available in a range of canvas size options.

aiItems.content:
What are abstract floral wall art prints?

Abstract floral wall art prints are artworks that draw inspiration from flowers, botanicals and plants but interpret them in a loose, expressive or stylised way — sitting somewhere between a precise botanical illustration and pure abstraction. They typically feature organic shapes, natural subjects such as blooms, stems and leaves, and a considered, often limited colour palette. This style has become hugely popular in UK homes because it brings the beauty of the natural world indoors without feeling overly literal or old-fashioned. A set of abstract floral prints is a versatile choice that works across many interior styles, from French Country and cottage to contemporary and Scandi-inspired spaces.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Abstract Floral Prints Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall space: Before ordering, measure the width of your chimney breast. For the best visual balance, aim for the three prints together to fill roughly two-thirds of the total width, with equal gaps between each one.

2. Choose your size: Use the size guide image on this page to see how small, medium and large options look in a real above-fireplace setting. When in doubt, go one size up — prints above a fireplace can often handle a larger size than you'd expect.

3. Mark your positions: Use a spirit level and a pencil to lightly mark where the top of each print will sit. Keep the gap between each print consistent — around 4–6 cm works well for a triptych like this — and make sure all three tops are perfectly level with each other.

4. Select your finish: Decide between an unframed print (great if you already have frames you love), a framed print (ready to hang straight away), or a wrapped canvas for a more textural, rustic feel.

5. Hang and style: Once your prints are up, step back and adjust the height if needed — the bottom of the prints should sit 15–20 cm above the mantel shelf. Style the mantel below with complementary accessories in natural tones to complete the French Country look.

Choosing Your Print Option — What's the Difference?

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A high-quality printed art print on Luster art paper. You choose and source your own frame. Great if you already have frames you love or want to match existing décor exactly. Printed in the UK with fade-resistant inks.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The same great UK-printed art print but on premium Museum quality paper for richer, deeper tones and exceptional detail — ideal if you want the very best reproduction of the ivory and charcoal botanical artwork. You source your own frame.

Framed Print — Your chosen art print comes already mounted and framed, arriving completely ready to hang. Saves you time and the hassle of finding a frame that fits. A brilliant choice if you want a polished, finished result with no extra effort.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a sturdy wooden stretcher frame — no additional frame needed. It arrives ready to hang and gives a lovely textural, tactile quality that suits rustic, cottage and French Country interiors beautifully.

How to Style wall pictures for hallway — Tips I Swear By

The hallway is the first room your guests see, so it is worth getting the art right. I would hang all three of these prints in a horizontal row at eye level, leaving an even gap between each one — roughly 5 to 8 cm works beautifully in most hallways. The ivory and charcoal palette is incredibly versatile: it looks stunning against warm white, soft sage, pale taupe, or even a deeper charcoal wall if you want to make more of a statement. Because the background of each print carries that warm ivory tone, the set also works a treat in narrower hallways where you want the space to feel light and airy rather than closed in.

If your hallway is longer, you could consider a staggered or slightly asymmetric arrangement — perhaps the centre print raised slightly higher for a more relaxed, French Country cottage feel. These prints also work wonderfully on a staircase wall going up in a diagonal line, each one leading the eye upward. For more styling ideas and inspiration on how to put a gallery wall together, have a browse through our botanical wall art collection — there are plenty of pieces that could sit alongside this set too.

Choosing the Right Size and Tone for Your Hallway

Hallways come in all shapes and sizes, and picking the right print size really does make a difference. In a narrow hallway, I would lean towards smaller or medium sizes so the three prints fit comfortably side by side without crowding the wall — something in the A4 to A3 range tends to work well. In a wider entrance hall or on a generous staircase wall, you can afford to go bigger and let the botanical details really breathe. The charcoal and ivory palette here is neutral enough that you do not need to worry too much about matching existing colours — these prints genuinely go with almost anything.

If you want the crispest possible detail in those delicate leaf veins and petal edges, the Museum quality paper option is worth considering — it gives a particularly clean, gallery-like finish. Luster is a lovely choice too if you prefer a slight sheen that brings out the contrast between the dark charcoal tones and the soft ivory backgrounds. Both options look beautiful; it really comes down to personal preference. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a hallway before you decide — there is a size-guide image below showing every available size displayed in that setting, which makes choosing so much easier.

What are wall pictures for hallway?

Wall pictures for hallway are art prints or framed artworks chosen specifically to decorate the entrance or corridor of a home, setting the tone and style the moment you walk through the door. They are typically sold in sets — such as a set of 3 — so the wall feels curated and cohesive rather than an afterthought. Good hallway wall art works with the available wall space, the lighting, and the existing colour palette of the home. Because hallways are often narrower and longer than other rooms, the best hallway prints tend to be portrait-oriented and work well displayed in a horizontal row or climbing a staircase wall. A botanical or floral set in neutral tones is a particularly popular choice as it suits a wide range of home styles, from French Country cottage to modern Scandi.

How to Hang Wall Pictures for Hallway — A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your wall space: Before you order, measure the width of the wall where you plan to hang the prints. For a set of 3, add together the total width of all three prints plus the gaps between them (allow 5–8 cm between each print) to make sure everything fits comfortably.

2. Choose your sizes: Use the size guide image on this page to see how each size looks in a real hallway setting. Narrower hallways suit smaller to medium sizes; wider entrance halls can carry larger prints with ease.

3. Mark your hanging points: Hold the first print against the wall at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print) and lightly mark the top with a pencil. Repeat for the other two prints, keeping the gaps even. A spirit level will be your best friend here.

4. Hang and check alignment: Hang all three prints, then step back and check they are level and evenly spaced before you are done. If you chose the framed or canvas-wrapped option, your prints arrive ready to hang — no extra frame hunting needed.

5. Adjust the styling: Once hung, stand at the end of the hallway and look at the set as a whole. Tiny adjustments in spacing or height can make a big difference to the finished look.

Comparing Your Options — Which Format Is Right for You?

Format — Unframed Print: You receive the art print only, ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Perfect if you have a specific frame style or colour in mind, or if you already have frames at home.

Format — Framed Print: Your print arrives ready to hang straight away — no frame shopping, no fuss. A great choice if you want a polished, finished look without the extra effort.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden frame, giving a contemporary gallery-style finish with no frame required. Ready to hang immediately.

Paper — Luster Art Paper: A semi-sheen finish that enhances contrast and gives a warm, photographic quality. Lovely for bringing out the depth in charcoal and ivory botanical illustrations like these.

Paper — Museum Quality Paper: A premium fine-art finish with a smooth, gallery-worthy surface that shows every fine detail in the botanical linework with exceptional clarity. Ideal if you want a truly special result.

aiItems.content:
What is a grey wall hanging?

A grey wall hanging is a piece of wall art — typically a print, canvas, or textile — that uses grey as its dominant or key colour, designed to be displayed on a wall as a decorative feature. Grey wall hangings are popular in offices and living spaces because grey is a genuinely versatile neutral that pairs with almost any other colour or material. They range from bold abstract designs to delicate botanical prints like this French Country set, which combines cool charcoal and soft grey plant illustrations on an ivory background. Choosing a grey wall hanging is a simple way to add visual interest and a calming atmosphere to a room without committing to a strong colour. Sets of three are particularly effective because they create a cohesive, gallery-style arrangement that feels intentional and complete.

How to Hang a Grey Wall Hanging Set of 3 in Your Office

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall that you face or look up at regularly — above a desk, behind a monitor, or on the wall opposite your chair. A plain, lighter-coloured wall lets the grey and ivory tones really sing.

2. Measure and mark: Lay all three prints on the floor first to plan your spacing. Aim for an even gap of 5–8 cm between each print. Measure the total combined width and mark the centre point on your wall with a pencil so you can centre the group.

3. Find the right height: Hang the centre of the arrangement at roughly eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor is a reliable guide for most people. If the prints sit above a desk, the bottom edge should be at least 20–25 cm above the desk surface.

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable with a row of three prints. A small spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone takes seconds and makes a real difference.

5. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back to the doorway and check the spacing and alignment from a distance before making any final adjustments.

Choosing Your Grey Wall Hanging Format — What's Right for You?

Finish options — Unframed print (print only, you choose your own frame or display as is); Framed print (arrives ready to hang, no extra shopping needed); Wrapped canvas (arrives ready to hang, no frame needed, contemporary edge-wrap look).

Paper / surface choice — Luster art paper (gentle sheen, rich grey tones, warm ivory feel); Museum quality paper (matte, gallery-like finish, pressed-botanical feel); Wrapped canvas (printed directly onto canvas, no paper choice needed).

Ready to hang? — Unframed print: no — you will need to source a frame or mount; Framed print: yes, straight out of the box; Wrapped canvas: yes, hanging hardware included.

Best for — Unframed: those who already have frames or want full control over the look; Framed: anyone who wants a hassle-free, complete result quickly; Wrapped canvas: those who prefer a more relaxed, contemporary display without a frame.

Metallic or foil finish? — None of our options include real metallic or foil finishes. Any warm or tonal variations in the artwork are printed tones only, faithfully reproduced on your chosen paper or canvas.
